foodDescription: A light, puffy dumpling of pike and flour paste, baked in a rich crayfish sauce. The signature dish of the bouchons.
A thick pork sausage, sometimes studded with pistachios, baked inside a loaf of brioche and served in slices.
Frisée lettuce with crisp bacon, croutons, and a soft poached egg, dressed with a sharp mustard vinaigrette.
“Silk worker’s brains,” a joke name for fresh white cheese beaten with herbs, shallots, oil, and vinegar. Eaten with bread or potatoes.
A coarse sausage of pork intestines, grilled and served with mustard. Strong-smelling and much loved by its fans.
“Fireman’s apron,” a slab of beef tripe marinated in white wine, breaded, and fried, served with garlic mayonnaise.
Thin-sliced potatoes baked slowly in cream and garlic until soft and golden. From the Dauphiné, just east of Lyon.
A tart filled with pink sugar-coated almonds melted down with cream into a sticky, bright pink filling.
Thin strips of dough fried and dusted with sugar, eaten around Mardi Gras.
A small green square of marzipan and chocolate, shaped like the silk cushion said to have held a candle offered to the Virgin during a plague in 1643.
A thick-bottomed 46-centiliter glass bottle in which bouchons serve house wine, usually Beaujolais or Côtes du Rhône.
A light, fruity red from the hills just north of Lyon, made from the Gamay grape. Locals say Lyon is watered by three rivers: the Rhône, the Saône, and the Beaujolais.
